messages.body_plain:

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

we will be having a Meet and Analyze Data session from 3:00pm-5:00pm
today (02/06),
in the Bennett Conference Room at the Center for Companion Animal Health
(http://campusmap.ucdavis.edu/?b=33).
Hope to see you there!

--

If you think you are going to join us, please let us know --

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeUW5QS55uDwDpusGYerY542D_tQubkmPMtUKlGdbmoSWfSSQ/viewform

--

Meet and Analyze Data (MAD) is a forum to bring your biological big
data and discuss high level concept problems (what is metagenome
assembly?) and low level coding problems (what does this error message
even mean?!) and everything in between. There is no scheduled or
specific activity: people show up with questions about how to analyze
their data, or maybe they are willing to help others. We typically get
questions about experimental design for
transcriptomic/metagenomic/genomic projects, or how to install
software, or how to run their analysis on clusters or the cloud.

Cheers,
Luiz Irber

messages.subject: Seeking a post-hoc for GLMs with beta distributions
messages.subject_clean: Seeking a post-hoc for GLMs with beta distributions
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I'm running some GLMs right now (real simple ones: y ~ x where "x" has 3 levels). My goal is to do the analogue to a traditional ANOVA + post-hoc to compare means across the 3 levels, only using non-normal distributions.

For the most part, my code is pretty straightforward. I've been writing my models using the "glm" function, running a likelihood ratio test as the ANOVA analogue, and then using the "glht" function from the "multcomp" library to run a Tukey post-hoc analogue. That post-hoc code looks like this:

summary( glht( glm.model, mcp( x="Tukey")))

Now I've run into an obstacle. Some of my response variables are proportions, and not the kind I can easily turn into binomials. So, I want to try using a beta distribution. To do this, I've been writing my model with the "betareg" function and again using a likelihood ratio test for the ANOVA analogue. However, for the post-hoc, the glht function doesn't support a betareg model with its "mcp" call.

Any suggestions?

Jan

Hi Corey,

There were a couple things going on here:

1) You were coding NA values as literally the character string "NA", which is not treated the same as actual NA values in R. Thus, your "na.rm = TRUE" arguments were not actually excluding anything, since you didn't have any true NAs in your "GIS" column to begin with.
2) Typically following a "group_by" command you're going to want a "summarize" function that creates new variables based on calculations performed over each of the groups you've specified.

This code is a bit verbose, but it'll get you there:

library(dplyr)

example <-
  data.frame(IDs = c(rep("A", 30), rep("B", 30)),

             timestamp = seq(c(ISOdate(2015, 10, 01)), by = "day", length.out = 60),

             trip = c(rep("1", 15), rep("2", 15)),

             GIS = c(rep("FOREST", 3), rep(NA_character_, 5),
                     rep("COAST", 3), rep(NA_character_, 4),
                     rep("FOREST", 7),rep(NA_character_, 8)
             )

  )

str(example) # shows that IDs, trip, and GIS are all factors.

temp.example <- example %>%

  mutate(GIS = as.character(GIS)) %>%

  arrange(IDs, timestamp) %>%
  group_by(IDs, trip) %>%

  summarize(
    distinct_non_NA_values = paste(na.omit(unique(GIS)), collapse = ", "),
    GIS = if_else(n_distinct(GIS, na.rm = TRUE) > 1,
                  "MIXED", distinct_non_NA_values)
    )

temp.example

Hope that helps!
Evan

messages.subject_clean: [D-RUG]: mutate using ifelse or if_else & n_distinct
messages.body_plain:
Hi Corey,

There are 3 challenges here:
1. n_distinct() returns one value per group, not per row, so you need to propagate its results across all of the rows in each group.
2. if_else() treats factors as integers rather than strings, and throws an error if the types don’t match. (Not an issue if you use ifelse()).
3. We need to propagate values to the NA rows.  (This assumes that missing values have the same real value as the other rows in their group.  I wouldn’t normally make this assumption in my own research, but I’ll assume that really is what you want to do here.)

We can address #1 by separating the n_distinct() and if_else() calls.  Use a grouped mutate to propagate the n_distinct() results, and then use if_else().

We can address #2 by coercing GIS to a character inside if_else().

And we can address #3 using zoo::locf(), “last observation carried forward," which propagates non-missing values downwards through the dataframe.  Note that this assumes we don’t have missing values at the top of each group!  IIRC something like arrange(IDs, trip, GIS) will put NAs at the end.  So that’s what I do here; but be sure to check that in your real data.

MWE:
> library(tidyverse)
> library(zoo)

>
> example <- data.frame(IDs = c(rep("A",30),rep("B",30)),
>                       timestamp = seq(c(ISOdate(2015,10,01)), by = "day", length.out = 60),
>                       trip = c(rep("1",15),rep("2",15)),
>                       GIS = c(rep("FOREST",3),rep(NA,5),rep("COAST",3),rep(NA,4),rep("FOREST",7),rep(NA,8)))
>

> example$GIStrip.desired <- c(rep("MIXED",15),rep("FOREST",15),rep("MIXED",15),rep("FOREST",15))
>
> example %>%
>     arrange(IDs, trip, GIS) %>%
>     ## Solution
>     group_by(IDs, trip) %>%
>     mutate(distinct = n_distinct(GIS, na.rm = TRUE),
>            GIStrip = if_else(distinct > 1,
>                             'MIXED',
>                             as.character(GIS)),
>            GIStrip = na.locf(GIStrip)) %>%
>     ungroup() %>%
>     ## Confirm works as expected
>     mutate(matches = GIStrip == GIStrip.desired) %>%
>     count(matches)
>
Cheers,
Dan

This is likely because you define the aes(z=value) in the first layers. So further layers are looking for that variable, even if irrelevant for next geometries. So either:
a) define the layer-specific aesthetics at the layer level
b) feed a dummy z value in the new dattaset

You unfortunately did not provide a reproducible example, but see below how to reproduce the error you get. Solution a) here is:    geom_tile(aes(fill=z), colour = "grey50")

df <- data.frame(
  x = rep(c(2, 5, 7, 9, 12), 2),
  y = rep(c(1, 2), each = 5),
  z = factor(rep(1:5, each = 2)),
  w = rep(diff(c(0, 4, 6, 8, 10, 14)), 2)
)

ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = z)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(data = select(df, -z), aes(x=x, y=y))
